doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: The Copacabana recording with Barry Manilow
summary: Recording Manilow's Copacabana in New York and L.A. with Paul Shaffer and Will Lee.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: How about the Copacabana recording at the Copa, tell us about how that came to be.

You know something? I wasn’t even sure we were recording that night you know. It was weird man because there was always gear around, people’s gear and mics and things you know, it was always around, lights. And I just played the show. It was like oh we’re just playing the show. You know.
But I mean I guess I didn’t explain, the Barry Manilow record at the Copa?
Oh yeah, yeah, I went to California for that.
Yeah. Were you with his band at the time or was that just —

No, no, it was just for the recordings. I did some recordings with him. I did some in New York and some in L.A. And Paul Shaffer was the leader and Will Lee playing bass. It was great, great players. But yeah that was some in New York and some out in L.A. And originally it started out where he wanted Copacabana to be like a Latin thing. Barry was at the piano, usually at the piano, and he’d start singing Copa Cobana [hums “Copacabana”] you know, he’s singing. And I don’t know it’s like this, it’s like that. And it was Latin. And then they hyped it up later. Then they decided, I think it was Clive Davis, they decided they wanted it strictly disco. And then they added stuff onto it. That’s the way that came about. But when we originally played it it was like Latin. But that became a huge hit.
Do you recall like thinking oh this is going to be a hit?
